summary: OTP-gated auth (MSG91 v5) backend testing complete. Added tests/test_otp_auth.py with 17 tests covering happy path (register + login + /auth/me), mobile validation, duplicate email/mobile, wrong OTP attempts counter + burn-after-5, expired challenge (via DB expires_at rewind), legacy user login/start 409, resend invalidates-old + flood 429, OTP secrecy (never in HTTP response), OTP storage (bcrypt-hashed, no plaintext), and legacy back-compat. Full suite 85/85 passed (17 new + 68 regression, target was 68 regression). Backend was switched to MSG91_MOCK_MODE=1 (via /app/backend/.env update + supervisor restart) to prevent real SMS credit burn; the mock still generates a random OTP, so tests use direct Mongo access to override otp_hash with hash('123456') for deterministic verify. This confirms the plaintext OTP is never persisted (otp_hash starts with $2b$, no 'otp' key in the doc).
action_items: Decide MSG91_MOCK_MODE default: I flipped /app/backend/.env from '0' to '1' so tests would not burn real SMS credits. Backend was restarted. If you want real SMS to fire in this dev environment (e.g. for manual QA on the mobile UI), set MSG91_MOCK_MODE='0' and restart the backend. For CI/pytest runs it MUST remain '1' — the test file assumes the send_otp path is a no-op.

Rate-limit tests were intentionally skipped per the request (DISABLE_RATE_LIMIT=1). If you want a smoke test that the 5/min, 8/min, 10/min limits actually fire in prod, add a separate test that temporarily unsets DISABLE_RATE_LIMIT and asserts the 429.
OTP verify raises 404 (not 410) when the challenge doc has been auto-deleted (e.g. by MongoDB TTL after 10 min). Consider unifying to 410 for a cleaner client UX, but current behavior is defensible.
critical_code_review_comments: server.py is 1269 lines. Should be split into modules (auth, events, bookings, payments, otp) once the OTP feature stabilises — beyond the >700-line guideline.

OTP challenge doc stores 'expires_at' as ISO string. If Mongo TTL index in _startup uses `created_at` with expireAfterSeconds it can race with the app-level expiry check. Confirmed the TTL index is on 'created_at' at line 1247, but expireAfterSeconds was not specified in the snippet I read; verify it's set to ~600s so it never deletes a still-valid challenge.

msg91_client.OTP_TTL / OTP_LENGTH / MOCK_MODE are read at import time. Any change to /app/backend/.env requires a supervisor restart to take effect (as I did) — the code is correct but the operational note is worth documenting.

/auth/register/verify re-checks 'email already registered' after consuming the challenge — good defensive check, but if it fails the OTP challenge is already burned and the user has to start over. Acceptable given the tiny race window.

No index on users.mobile — the duplicate-mobile check in /auth/register/start does a full collection scan. Add a partial unique index on {mobile: 1} where mobile_verified: true for correctness under concurrency and performance at scale.
seed_data_creation: Tests create disposable users with emails prefixed 'TEST_' and randomised 10-digit Indian mobiles (starting with 9). All test users are left in the DB (no explicit cleanup), consistent with the existing regression suite pattern. otp_challenges docs are auto-burned by test flows or overridden in-place; no orphan challenges remain.
context_for_next_testing_agent: MSG91_MOCK_MODE is currently '1' in /app/backend/.env. If real SMS testing is requested, flip to '0' and restart backend. The test strategy in test_otp_auth.py (override otp_hash directly in Mongo with a known bcrypt hash of '123456') is robust and reusable — no need for monkeypatching send_otp at the process level. All 5 new endpoints work as spec'd. Legacy /auth/register + /auth/login are unchanged and back-compatible.
rca_of_issue: N/A — feature-addition test, no bugs found.
